source.title: Characterization and Mitigation of Training Instabilities in Microscaling Formats
source.authors: Huang-Yuan Su; Mujin Kwun; Stephanie Gil; S. Kakade; Nikhil Anand

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests empirical loss-scaling fits in the new setting of microscaling and hybrid-precision language-model pretraining; it is not a reproduction of the original scaling-law studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling fits for several precision configurations and reports that fully quantized MX runs often become unstable. It also cites scaling-law findings from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Individual validation-loss differences in Tables 1, 4 and 5 are omitted because the flattened multi-column text does not safely align every value with its model and precision condition.
record.test_reason: The study trains about 70 OLMo models per precision configuration from scratch (~20M–1.7B params, 2e17–~1e19 FLOPs). It fits the Hoffmann/Chinchilla loss form L(N,D)=E+A/N^α+B/D^β to stabilised runs and reports the exponents and a=β/(α+β). These fits are a new-setting (low-precision MX training) result on V1 and V3. They are a secondary, 'proof of concept' part of a paper mainly about training instabilities.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find that fully quantised MX training (MXFP8/MXFP6) often causes unrecoverable instabilities, which they trace to multiplicative gradient bias from clamping of clustered layer-norm affine weights and a small fraction of activations. Keeping activations in bfloat16 or quantising only the forward pass stabilises OLMo training and allows Chinchilla-style scaling fits, presented as a proof of concept at the tested scales. MXFP8 E4M3 weights with bf16 activations match bfloat16 performance. The authors caution that results may not extrapolate an order of magnitude larger.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Chinchilla-style loss function to fit validation loss across OLMo parameter/token/compute sweeps under MX and hybrid precision; it is not a reproduction of the original scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Stability and the ability to fit scaling laws change with precision configuration and whether quantization is applied in the backward pass; the paper also reports instability dependence on learning rate, architecture and activation choices in its proxy experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully quantised MX training (forward and backward, weights and activations) produces sharp, unrecoverable loss divergences, mainly in larger, longer-trained models. The authors say this prevents extracting valid scaling laws.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training stability under low-precision formats is a precondition for observing loss scaling laws. Instabilities grow with scale and training length.

record.problems: The language-model sweeps use relatively small models (largest ∼1.7B parameters); the authors caution that results may not extrapolate to models an order of magnitude larger. Experiments emulate MX formats in software rather than on Blackwell-class hardware. Fit uncertainties are not reported in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Individual validation-loss differences from Table 1 and Tables 4–5 are not extracted: the flattened multi-column text does not safely align all values with each model size and precision condition. The fits and coefficients reported in Table 2, plus the relevant figure-only result, are retained.

untested.parts: Scales beyond ~1.7B params / ~1e19 FLOPs. Fit residuals or goodness-of-fit are not reported. Only about two orders of magnitude in compute are covered.
Not tested: no fit on small runs is checked against much larger runs.
Exponent b for tokens is not reported separately. There is no direct comparison to Kaplan allocation and no IsoFLOP or other allocation method.
Not tested. Low-precision training is still text pretraining.
Not tested. Only one fitting method is used, with no uncertainties, so the small exponent differences across precisions cannot be judged.

missing.what: Fit quality: residuals, R² or bootstrap CIs on α, β, a. Without these, cross-precision exponent differences cannot be assessed.
missing.locator: Appendix C, Table 2 and Figures 8, 12, 13 (not reported in paper)

missing.what: Per-run bfloat16 validation losses showing loss falling with compute (e.g. ~1.10 at 2e17 to ~0.72 at 1e19 FLOPs at the best D/N). These were declared left out, but they are the raw data behind the V1 fit.

record.verdict_notes: Removed the reader's V1 'challenges' label on r8: divergence is a training failure, not evidence against power-law loss scaling. Removed the V7 'supports' label: exponent spreads of ~0.03 without uncertainties do not show setup dependence, and if anything a is stable across precisions. The paper labels its fitted loss inconsistently: validation loss in the text, 'Train Loss' on figure axes. MXFP6 labelling also conflicts between Table 2 and Figure 13b. Scaling fits are secondary to the paper's instability focus.

versions.untested_parts: The tests concern OLMo pretraining and the reported precision configurations and scales only; they do not establish the claim for other models or arbitrary training setups.
No experiment fits laws on small runs and then evaluates predictions against substantially larger runs.
The paper fits a Chinchilla-style loss function and reports the exponent for optimal model size relative to FLOPs; it does not directly compare against Kaplan et al. or test other allocation setups.
No controlled comparison of depth, width or other architecture details at fixed parameter count for language-model loss.
No scaling-law tests in other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning or transfer.
No downstream-task performance measurements or downstream prediction from pretraining loss.
The fits compare precision configurations, not alternative fitting procedures, parameter-counting conventions or the broader published-law disagreements and curve bending described in the version.

rows.subject: OLMo sweep, MXFP6 E2M3 weights / bfloat16 activations
rows.size_stated: The language-model sweep ranges from ∼20M to ∼1.7B parameters; Table 1 also lists model sizes from 0.16B to 0.54B.
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss to the Chinchilla-style function of parameter count and training tokens; quantize MX in the forward and backward passes as applicable.
rows.measure: Fitted loss-scaling parameters; the final value is a = β/(α + β), the exponent of optimal model size relative to FLOPs.
rows.note: One fit for this precision configuration.
rows.check: Drop the V7 link: near-identical exponents across precisions with no uncertainties cannot show fit-dependence. Labelling conflict: Table 2 calls this config MXFP6 E2M3 weights with bfloat16 activations. Figure 13b, which seems to be its only plotted fit, is labelled full MXFP6 E2M3/E2M3, and Appendix F says no fully low-precision combination was stable. The subject is therefore uncertain.

rows.subject: OLMo sweeps, fully quantized MX configurations
rows.size_stated: Approximately 70 models per configuration; ∼20M to ∼1.7B parameters.
rows.operation_detail: Train with MX quantization of weights and activations in both forward and backward passes; report training-loss instabilities and divergence.

conditions.value: Multiple MXFP8 and MXFP6 weight–activation combinations

rows.measure: Whether training loss remains stable and permits a valid scaling-law fit.
rows.baseline: bfloat16 training remains stable with smooth convergence and bounded gradients.
rows.value: The authors report frequent sharp, unrecoverable instabilities, especially in larger, longer-trained models, and say they were generally unable to find stable lower-precision weight–activation combinations across the tested formats.
rows.locator: Sections 3.2 and 7; Figures 1, 16 and 17; Appendix F
rows.note: Aggregate description across the tested fully quantized MX sweeps; the paper states that unstable runs cannot yield valid scaling laws.
rows.check: This row measures training stability and divergence, not how loss scales with N, D or C. Failed runs do not show the power law is absent; they only prevent a fit. Move it to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: OLMo on Fineweb-Edu, bfloat16 and stabilised MXFP8 configs (bf16 activations or forward-only quantisation), ~20M–1.7B params, 2e17–~1e19 FLOPs
relationships.reason: Chinchilla-form power-law fits are obtained with α≈0.49–0.52 and β≈0.51–0.59 (r1–r6). However, no fit-quality measure is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Chinchilla-form power-law fits yielded α ≈ 0.49–0.52 and β ≈ 0.51–0.59 across the tested precision configurations.
